DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
## What the paper argues

The paper recommends awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months. Its case rests on four points:
- ParcelLine is cheapest at the 70/30 weight mix, saving about £35,000–£76,000 a year.
- All three carriers met the 95% on-time requirement in a randomised two-month trial.
- ParcelLine's tracking app roughly halves "where is my order?" contacts.
- The 12-month term preserves flexibility.

I checked every figure against the paper's own tables. The price arithmetic is correct. But Table 1 shows ParcelLine **failing two of the paper's four stated requirements**. Once the paper's own £48 cost per damaged or lost parcel is applied, ParcelLine becomes the **most expensive** option rather than the cheapest.

## What is sound

**The trial design is genuinely strong.**
- Parcels were allocated at random by the warehouse system.
- Each carrier handled about 5,000 parcels.
- Outcomes were measured against promised dates and customer reports.

The author is right that this makes it a fair head-to-head.

**The price arithmetic is correct:**

| Carrier | Average cost per parcel | Monthly cost |
|---|---|---|
| SwiftDrop | £3.55 | £149,100 |
| ParcelLine | £3.48 | £146,160 |
| Meridian | £3.63 | £152,460 |

The annual differences of £35,280 and £75,600 are also correct.

**The contact-handling saving is calculated correctly.** ParcelLine's saving against SwiftDrop is 210 fewer contacts × £3.20 ≈ £670 a month.

**The 12-month term is a real advantage** of ParcelLine and SwiftDrop over Meridian's 24 months.

## 1. ParcelLine failed two of the four requirements

| Requirement (§2) | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| On-time ≥ 95% | 96.2% ✓ | **93.1% ✗** | 97.5% ✓ |
| Damage < 0.5% | 0.4% ✓ | **0.9% ✗** | 0.3% ✓ |

- §3, the Recommendation and the author's description all say every carrier cleared the on-time threshold. Table 1 shows ParcelLine at **93.1%**, below the 95% requirement.
- ParcelLine's damage rate is **0.9%**, almost double the 0.5% limit. The paper doesn't mention this.
- These shortfalls aren't noise:
  - With about 5,000 parcels, the on-time figure is precise to roughly ±0.7 points, so 93.1% is clearly below 95%.
  - The damage difference is about 45 damaged parcels against 15–20 for the other two carriers.

## 2. Including the paper's own damage and loss costs reverses the ranking

§2 states that each damaged or lost parcel costs £48. Applied to 42,000 parcels a month, with the contact-handling costs from §5 added:

| Monthly | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivery | £149,100 | £146,160 | £152,460 |
| Damage + loss (rate × 42,000 × £48) | £8,669 | £19,757 | £6,451 |
| "Where is my order?" contacts (× £3.20) | £1,478 | £806 | £1,344 |
| **Total** | **£159,247** | **£166,723** | **£160,255** |

**On these figures:**
- ParcelLine costs about **£7,500 a month more than SwiftDrop**, roughly £90,000 a year. It costs about £6,500 a month more than Meridian.
- **SwiftDrop is cheapest overall**, about £1,000 a month below Meridian.
- The £35,000–£76,000 "saving" is reversed into a cost of about £78,000–£90,000 a year.

**The loss figures rest on tiny counts.** With about 5,000 parcels, rates of 2–8 per 10,000 mean only about 1–4 lost parcels per carrier. Those rates are too imprecise to compare. But dropping losses entirely doesn't change the conclusion. ParcelLine's damage cost alone is about £18,100 a month, against about £8,100 for SwiftDrop and £6,000 for Meridian.

**This leaves out a further cost.** The paper notes that damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews. That reputational cost is on top of the £48.

## 3. The drop in contacts can't be credited to the tracking app

- From 1 May, half-way through the trial, **only ParcelLine parcels carried your new proactive delivery-day text**. A text telling customers when their parcel will arrive is exactly the kind of thing that reduces "where is my order?" contacts.
- The data can't separate the text's effect from the app's. So "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" isn't supported.
- **The advantage may also disappear.** If the text is rolled out to every carrier as planned, the others' contact rates may fall too.
- Splitting ParcelLine's contact rate into April (no text) and May (with text) would show how much the app contributes on its own.

## 4. Peak-season risk

- The contract starts on 1 October, straight into the November–December peak.
- The trial ran in April–May.
- SwiftDrop and Meridian have handled peak volumes for retailers of similar size. ParcelLine's references are mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.
- 30% of your volume is 2–10 kg items such as lamps, mirrors and small furniture, which are fragile and heavier.
- ParcelLine's high damage rate may be concentrated in that heavier band. A damage breakdown by weight would show whether it is.

## 5. Smaller points

- **"Barely half."** ParcelLine's contacts were 55–60% of the other carriers' (6 against 10–11 per 1,000). Close enough, but it's the confounding issue in point 3 that matters.
- **Sample size.** About 5,000 parcels per carrier is enough for on-time and damage rates. It isn't enough for loss rates, as noted above.
- **Meridian.** It performed best on every service measure but requires a 24-month term. That trade-off is worth a sentence in the paper.

## What I'd ask the author to fix before the decision

1. Correct the on-time statement: ParcelLine scored 93.1%, below the 95% requirement.
2. Report ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate against the 0.5% requirement.
3. Add damage and loss costs at £48 per parcel to the cost comparison, and re-rank the carriers.
4. Separate the effect of the delivery-day text from the app, using April and May separately.
5. Break down damage by weight band and address peak-season readiness.

## Bottom line

The trial is a good one, and its results point away from ParcelLine. ParcelLine missed both the on-time and damage requirements. Applying the paper's own £48 cost per incident turns its £35,000–£76,000 saving into an extra cost of roughly £78,000–£90,000 a year. Its contact advantage is confounded with your own delivery-day text.

On the paper's data, **SwiftDrop** is the strongest candidate:
- it meets every requirement;
- it is cheapest once damage is counted;
- it offers the same 12-month term;
- it has peak-season experience with retailers of your size.

**Meridian** is the alternative if the board values the best service figures over the shorter term.
